Benchmark on eight eukaryotes

This notebook supports three parts of the manuscript:

  • Methods, benchmark data, compared methods and accuracy measures (../manuscript/sections/methods_benchmark.tex);
  • Results, accuracy across eight eukaryotes, with Table tab:bench (Table 1) (../manuscript/sections/results_benchmark.tex);
  • Fig. 2 (fig:benchmark, figures/fig2_benchmark.{pdf,png}), a ggplot2 port of figures/fig2_benchmark/make_fig2.py.

Provenance: E07 (benchmark design, inputs, comparator versions and commands), E25 (release reruns of TransDecoder and PyTD), E16 (how the comparator papers benchmarked; background only, no numbers are taken from it here).

Which runs. TransDecoder appears in the benchmark under two sets of labels:

  • earlier final defaults: pytd_dev_v2 / perl_td_dev_v2 (PyTD 48c870c, Perl de3f57e; fixed short-ORF test; E07). The manuscript text, Table 1 and the current Fig. 2 quote these runs.
  • release: pytd_v7 / perl_td_v7 (PyTD main 3a793ff, Perl devel 41fc5ee; decoy q-value test at q 0.05; E25), with the presets pytd_v7_precise, pytd_v7_sensitive and the homology runs pytd_v7_homology.

Figures, Table 1 and the numbers written here use the release runs (pytd_v7). The checks at the end compare them with the text as it stands, so a mismatch for a TransDecoder number shows a value the text must update. The section “Release versus earlier final defaults” lists the earlier values next to the release values. TransDecoder v6.0.0 is an older release that the text compares explicitly, so it is kept.

S <- read_tab("benchmark", SUMMARY_FILE)
A7 <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "all_scores.tsv")
IDENT <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "perl_pytd_identity.tsv")
NEG <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "negatives_scores.tsv")

TD <- "pytd_v7"; TD_PERL <- "perl_td_v7"; TD_OLD <- "pytd_dev_v2"
INPUTS <- S %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% distinct(org, variant)
N_INPUTS <- nrow(INPUTS)

# value of one metric for one tool and variant, named by organism (in ORGS order; NA if missing)
V <- function(tool, variant, metric) {
  d <- S[S$tool == tool & S$variant == variant, ]
  setNames(d[[metric]][match(ORGS, d$org)], ORGS)
}
MED <- function(tool, variant, metric) median(V(tool, variant, metric), na.rm = TRUE)
r3 <- function(x) round(x, 3)
rng <- function(x) paste0(f3(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)), "-", f3(max(x, na.rm = TRUE)))

The summary is interim. Rows missing for the tools used here:

  • CodAn: 5 of 84 inputs have no row: human complete.wLnc; human fragments.wLnc; mouse complete.wLnc; mouse fragments.wLnc; tthermophila complete.unstranded.wRand. The T. thermophila complete.unstranded.wRand run was still running; CodAn has no lncRNA (wLnc) runs. None of these inputs is used in Fig. 2 or Table 1, which use the stranded complete, complete + random and fragments inputs; CodAn has all 8 organisms there.
  • PyTD with homology (pytd_v7_homology): 32 of 84 rows (athal 10, creinhardtii 10, dmel 10, human 2); the other runs were still running. These runs are not in Fig. 2 or Table 1; the section on homology below uses the available rows only.
  • --precise and --sensitive were run on the negative-containing inputs only (20 each; E25).
  • RNAsamba was run on stranded inputs only (44); v6.0.0, v5.7.1 and the longest-ORF baseline have no lncRNA inputs (80); ANGEL has 3 runs (dropped, Methods).

Agreement with the release score table (E25)

data/benchmark/final_v7/all_scores.tsv was scored with score_v7.sh from the same runs (E25).

Genetic-code compatibility

T. thermophila reads TAA and TAG as glutamine. GeneMarkS-T (tables 1, 4 and 11 only), CodAn, CPC2, RNAsamba and Borf have no option for this code; they were run with the standard code, so their T. thermophila results show only that the code is unsupported. These tool × organism results are excluded from everything below (reported as not applicable): Fig. 2 marks them “n/a”, their Table 1 medians are over the other seven organisms, and the rankings leave out T. thermophila. Their values are listed here and kept in S_raw (also used for run times, which do not depend on the code). TransDecoder (-G Tetrahymena), Prodigal (-g 6) and CPAT (TGA as the only stop) were run with the ciliate code.

INCOMPATIBLE <- c("gmst", "codan", "cpc2", "rnasamba", "borf")
S_raw <- S
S <- S %>% filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE))
details(S_raw %>% filter(org == "tthermophila", tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE,
                         variant %in% c("complete", "fragments", "complete.wRand")) %>%
          select(tool, variant, f1_stop, f1_exact, precision_stop) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), r3)),
        "excluded: standard-code tools on T. thermophila (stranded inputs)")

  • Eight organisms; truth-set sizes from 5,100 (S. pombe) to 26,867 (A. thaliana) genes. Every input of an organism has the same n_truth.

Accuracy measures (Methods)

The scoring rules (stop within 2 nt; exact within 2 nt at both ends) are applied by score_predictions.py (E07). Runtimes are wall-clock seconds per run (runtime_sec) under 6-16 concurrent jobs on a shared 28-core host (E07); the concurrency is from the launch logs, not from a table here.

Table 1: benchmark accuracy

Median over the eight organisms, stranded inputs: stop and exact F1 on complete and fragments, and stop-level precision on complete + random (complete.wRand). For the tools that do not support the ciliate code, the medians are over the other seven organisms (T. thermophila not applicable).

TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder (release)", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0",
           longest_orf = "longest ORF", prodigal = "Prodigal", gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", cpat = "CPAT",
           rnasamba = "RNAsamba", cpc2 = "CPC2", borf = "Borf", codan = "CodAn")
COLS <- tribble(~col, ~variant, ~metric,
                "complete_stop_f1", "complete", "f1_stop",
                "complete_exact_f1", "complete", "f1_exact",
                "fragments_stop_f1", "fragments", "f1_stop",
                "fragments_exact_f1", "fragments", "f1_exact",
                "complete_rand_precision", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
tab1_long <- tidyr::crossing(tool = names(TOOLS), COLS) %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(median = MED(tool, variant, metric), n_orgs = sum(!is.na(V(tool, variant, metric)))) %>% ungroup()
table1 <- tab1_long %>% select(tool, col, median) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = median) %>%
  left_join(tab1_long %>% group_by(tool) %>% summarise(min_orgs = min(n_orgs)), by = "tool") %>%
  mutate(label = TOOLS[tool], tool = factor(tool, levels = names(TOOLS))) %>% arrange(tool) %>%
  mutate(tool = as.character(tool),
         note = case_when(tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE ~ "7 organisms (ciliate code not supported)",
                          min_orgs < 8 ~ sprintf("interim: %d of 8 organisms in some column", min_orgs),
                          TRUE ~ "")) %>%
  select(tool, label, all_of(COLS$col), min_orgs, note)
write_tsv(table1 %>% mutate(across(all_of(COLS$col), ~ round(.x, 4))),
          data_path("benchmark", "final_v7", "table1.tsv"))
T1 <- function(tool, col) table1[[col]][table1$tool == tool]
kableExtra::kable_styling(kable(table1 %>% select(-tool, -min_orgs) %>% mutate(across(all_of(COLS$col), r3)),
  col.names = c("method", "complete stop F1", "complete exact F1", "fragments stop F1", "fragments exact F1",
                "complete + rand precision", "note"),
  caption = sprintf("Table 1 (from %s; written to data/benchmark/final_v7/table1.tsv)", SUMMARY_FILE)),
  full_width = FALSE)

Fig. 2: accuracy on eight eukaryotes

Stranded inputs, organisms ordered by transcriptome G+C. Panels a-e are heatmaps (colour clipped at 0.4); panel f is the run time on complete inputs, median and range over organisms. Cells marked “n/a” are tools that do not support the ciliate code on T. thermophila (GeneMarkS-T, CodAn, CPC2, RNAsamba, Borf; not applicable, above); grey cells marked “pend.” are rows missing from the summary. TransDecoder is the release default (pytd_v7, identical to perl_td_v7).

HEAT_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0", prodigal = "Prodigal",
                gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
                borf = "Borf", longest_orf = "longest ORF")
WRONG_CODE <- c("gmst", "codan", "cpc2", "rnasamba", "borf")
PANELS <- tribble(~panel, ~variant, ~metric, ~title,
                  "a", "complete", "f1_stop", "complete: stop-level F1",
                  "b", "complete", "f1_exact", "complete: exact F1",
                  "c", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop", "complete + random: precision",
                  "d", "fragments", "f1_stop", "fragments: stop-level F1",
                  "e", "fragments", "f1_exact", "fragments: exact F1")
ORG_SHORT <- c(pfalciparum = "P. fal.", tthermophila = "T. the.", spombe = "S. pom.", athal = "A. tha.",
               dmel = "D. mel.", mouse = "M. mus.", human = "H. sap.", creinhardtii = "C. rei.")
heat <- tidyr::crossing(PANELS, tool = names(HEAT_TOOLS), org = ORGS) %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(value = V(tool, variant, metric)[[org]]) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(wrong = org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% WRONG_CODE,
         x = match(org, ORGS), y = length(HEAT_TOOLS) + 1 - match(tool, names(HEAT_TOOLS)),
         lab = ifelse(wrong, "n/a", ifelse(is.na(value), "pend.", ifelse(round(value, 2) >= 1, "1.0", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", value))))))
n_pending <- sum(is.na(heat$value) & !heat$wrong)

RT_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "PyTD", perl_td_v7 = "TD (Perl)", prodigal = "Prodigal",
              gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
              borf = "Borf", angel = "ANGEL")
rt <- S_raw %>% filter(variant == "complete", tool %in% names(RT_TOOLS)) %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(median = median(runtime_sec), min = min(runtime_sec), max = max(runtime_sec), n = n()) %>%
  mutate(label = RT_TOOLS[tool], y = length(RT_TOOLS) + 1 - match(tool, names(RT_TOOLS)),
         note = case_when(tool == "angel" ~ sprintf("%.0f h (A. thal.)", median / 3600),
                          median > 3600 ~ sprintf("%.1f h%s", median / 3600, ifelse(n == 8, "", sprintf("  (n = %d)", n))),
                          TRUE ~ paste0(num(round(median)), " s", ifelse(n == 8, "", sprintf("  (n = %d)", n)))))
heat_fill <- scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#f7fbff", "#c6dbef", "#6baed6", "#2171b5", "#08306b"),
                                  limits = c(0.4, 1), oob = scales::squish, breaks = c(0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1),
                                  labels = c("≤0.4", "0.6", "0.8", "1.0"), name = "F1 or precision",
                                  na.value = "#dddddd")
hatch <- function(d) {   # diagonal lines inside each hatched cell
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
  offs <- seq(-0.8, 0.8, by = 0.2)
  segs <- tidyr::crossing(d %>% select(x, y), o = offs) %>%
    mutate(x0 = pmax(-0.5, -0.5 + o), y0 = pmax(-0.5, -0.5 - o), x1 = pmin(0.5, 0.5 + o), y1 = pmin(0.5, 0.5 - o)) %>%
    filter(x1 > x0)
  geom_segment(data = segs, aes(x = x + x0, y = y + y0, xend = x + x1, yend = y + y1),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#aaaaaa", linewidth = 0.15)
}
heat_panel <- function(p, show_rows) {
  d <- heat %>% filter(panel == p)
  ok <- d %>% filter(!wrong)
  ggplot(ok, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = value), colour = NA) +
    geom_tile(data = d %>% filter(wrong), fill = "#f2f2f2", colour = NA) +
    geom_text(aes(label = lab, colour = !is.na(value) & (pmin(value, 1) - 0.4) / 0.6 > 0.55), size = 1.62) +
    geom_text(data = d %>% filter(wrong), aes(label = lab), colour = "#888888", size = 1.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "#222222"), guide = "none") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = length(HEAT_TOOLS) + 0.5 - c(2, 5, 9), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    heat_fill +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(ORGS), labels = ORG_SHORT[ORGS], expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(HEAT_TOOLS), labels = if (show_rows) rev(HEAT_TOOLS) else NULL,
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = PANELS$title[PANELS$panel == p]) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust = 1, face = "italic", size = 5.6),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6), axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
}
rt_panel <- ggplot(rt, aes(y = y)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = min, xend = max, yend = y, colour = tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(x = median, colour = tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)), size = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(x = pmax(max, median) * 1.35, label = note), hjust = 0, size = 1.9, colour = "#444444") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = TD_C, `FALSE` = "#6b6b6b"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(limits = c(5, 3e7), breaks = c(10, 1e3, 1e5), labels = c("10 s", expression(10^3~s), expression(10^5~s))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = rt$y, labels = rt$label) +
  labs(x = "wall-clock time (log scale)", y = NULL,
       title = "run time, complete inputs") +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))
fig2 <- (heat_panel("a", TRUE) + heat_panel("b", FALSE) + heat_panel("c", FALSE) +
         heat_panel("d", TRUE) + heat_panel("e", FALSE) + rt_panel) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3, guides = "collect") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(8, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(2.5, "mm"),
        legend.title.position = "top")
png_f <- save_fig(fig2, "fig2_benchmark", FULL_W, 128 * MM)
fig2

    pivot_wider(names_from = org, values_from = value)

}

Implementations: Perl and Python

n_ident <- sum(IDENT$identical)
pp <- S %>% filter(tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)) %>% select(org, variant, tool, all_of(setdiff(metric_cols, "runtime_sec"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(org, variant, tool)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = tool)
n_score_diff <- sum(pp[[TD]] != pp[[TD_PERL]])
ratio <- S %>% filter(tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)) %>% select(org, variant, tool, runtime_sec) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = tool, values_from = runtime_sec) %>% mutate(ratio = .data[[TD_PERL]] / .data[[TD]])
ratio_c <- ratio %>% filter(variant == "complete")
rt_med <- function(tool) median(S$runtime_sec[S$tool == tool & S$variant == "complete"])
ident_rt <- IDENT %>% inner_join(ratio, by = c("org", "variant"))
stopifnot(all(abs(ident_rt$perl_runtime_sec - ident_rt[[TD_PERL]]) < 1e-6),
          all(abs(ident_rt$pytd_runtime_sec - ident_rt[[TD]]) < 1e-6))
  • Predictions of the Perl and Python release versions are identical in 84 of 84 inputs (perl_pytd_identity.tsv: sorted preds.tsv compared, E25), and all score columns agree (0 differing cells). One set of numbers describes both implementations.
  • Run time, Perl / Python: median ratio 2.71 (2.07-3.28) over the 84 inputs; on complete inputs 2.57. Median run time on complete inputs: Python 281 s, Perl 717 s (earlier final defaults: 185 s and 422 s). Shared host, indicative only. The 2.3-fold figure in the abstract and in Results, algorithm, is for the earlier runs and is checked in 01_algorithm.Rmd.

Accuracy across eight eukaryotes

The text opens by stating that the Perl and Python implementations gave identical predictions; see the section above (84/84 inputs, release versions). E25

Stop codons

td_cs <- V(TD, "complete", "f1_stop"); v6_cs <- V("perl_td_v600", "complete", "f1_stop")
lo_cs <- V("longest_orf", "complete", "f1_stop")
td_v6_maxdiff <- max(abs(td_cs - v6_cs))

On complete transcripts, the release default had a stop-level F1 of 0.933-0.997 (median 0.980), against 0.948-0.985 for v6.0.0 and 0.954-0.984 for the longest-ORF baseline. Per organism, the release default was within 0.014 of v6.0.0 at the stop level. E07, E25

Noncoding sequence

td_p <- V(TD, "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
pr_p <- V("prodigal", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
lo_p <- V("longest_orf", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
cp_p <- V("cpat", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")

With one GC-matched random sequence per transcript, the release default kept a median stop-level precision of 0.994 (0.980-0.997), and its median stop F1 went from 0.980 to 0.979. Prodigal’s precision was 0.344-0.866 (median 0.660), and its median stop F1 went from 0.937 to 0.791. The longest-ORF baseline had a median precision of 0.803 (C. reinhardtii 0.567). RNAsamba 0.721, Borf 0.838; CPAT 0.971 (C. reinhardtii 0.629).

Start codons

td_ce <- V(TD, "complete", "f1_exact"); v6_ce <- V("perl_td_v600", "complete", "f1_exact")
cls_ce <- sapply(c("cpat", "rnasamba", "cpc2"), MED, variant = "complete", metric = "f1_exact")
cls_fe <- sapply(c("cpat", "rnasamba", "cpc2"), MED, variant = "fragments", metric = "f1_exact")

The longest-ORF baseline had a median exact F1 of 0.689. The release default had an exact F1 of 0.747-0.940 on complete transcripts (median 0.912), against 0.567-0.912 (median 0.779) for v6.0.0. Prodigal median 0.643, GeneMarkS-T 0.783. CPAT, RNAsamba and CPC2: medians 0.935-0.961 on complete transcripts and 0.183-0.486 on fragments (TransDecoder 0.822).

Run with the standard code, GeneMarkS-T, RNAsamba, CPC2 and Borf had F1 of at most 0.020 on T. thermophila (stranded complete and fragments). CodAn, also with the standard code: stop F1 NA (complete) and NA (fragments). With the ciliate code, the release default reached a stop F1 of 0.933 and an exact F1 of 0.833 on complete transcripts; v6.0.0 0.948 / 0.567, Prodigal 0.856 / 0.395, CPAT 0.884 / 0.851. Precision with random sequences: 0.980 (release default), 0.519 (v6.0.0), 0.344 (Prodigal).

GC extremes

cre_others <- sapply(c("perl_td_v600", "prodigal", "gmst", "cpat"), function(t) V(t, "complete", "f1_exact")[["creinhardtii"]])

P. falciparum: exact F1 0.940 (highest of the eight: P. falciparum), stop F1 0.997. C. reinhardtii: stop F1 0.975, exact F1 0.747 (lowest: C. reinhardtii). Other methods on C. reinhardtii (v6.0.0, Prodigal, GeneMarkS-T, CPAT): exact F1 0.653-0.786.

Fragments by partial type

Each fragment keeps either the 3’ piece of the transcript (stop present, start lost: a 5’ partial CDS) or the 5’ piece (start present, stop lost: a 3’ partial CDS), about half each. For a 3’ partial the reference 3’ end is the last whole codon at the fragment end, so a stop-level match means the prediction runs to the fragment end; for a 5’ partial an exact match means it starts at the fragment start (no start codon). Table from pipeline/derive/02_partial_types.py (same matching as score_predictions.py; summed over the two types it reproduces every true-positive count of the summary). Stranded fragments, median over organisms (seven for the tools that do not support the ciliate code). Precision is over predictions on fragments of that type. Fragments with both ends missing (internal) are scored in the balanced mixed inputs (next section).

PT <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "partial_types.tsv") %>%
  filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE))
PT_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0", prodigal = "Prodigal",
              gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
              borf = "Borf", longest_orf = "longest ORF")
pt <- PT %>% filter(variant == "fragments", tool %in% names(PT_TOOLS)) %>%
  mutate(type = recode(type, `5prime_partial` = "5' partial (start lost)", `3prime_partial` = "3' partial (stop lost)")) %>%
  group_by(tool, type) %>%
  summarise(n_org = n(), across(c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), median), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(method = factor(PT_TOOLS[tool], levels = PT_TOOLS)) %>% arrange(method, type)
pt_wide <- pt %>% select(method, type, sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), names_glue = "{type}: {.value}")
kable(pt_wide %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), r3)))

PTV <- function(tool, type, m) pt[[m]][pt$tool == tool & grepl(paste0("^", type), pt$type)]

TransDecoder: on 3’ partials stop-level sensitivity 0.877, exact 0.816; on 5’ partials 0.871 and 0.735. Prodigal: 3’ partials 0.955 / 0.650, 5’ partials 0.940 / 0.937. The classifiers that require an ATG (CPAT, CPC2, RNAsamba) have exact sensitivity of at most 0.018 on 5’ partials.

Balanced mixed inputs

The fragments inputs hold one partial type per sequence and no complete transcripts, and have no internal fragments (both ends missing). Methods that train on their input (TransDecoder’s coding and start models, GeneMarkS-T, Prodigal) are affected by such a composition. The balanced mixed inputs fragments_mixed_t1, _t2 and _t3 (pipeline/benchmark/make_mixed_inputs.py, E28) are built from the same transcripts as fragments (UTRs at most 250 nt). Each one assigns every transcript at random to one of four equal groups:

  • complete (unchanged);
  • 5’ partial: cut inside codons 2 to 80% of the CDS, uniformly, keeping the 3’ piece;
  • 3’ partial: cut from 20% of the CDS to just before the stop codon, uniformly, keeping the 5’ piece;
  • internal: a window of about half the CDS (fraction from \(\mathcal N(0.5,0.1)\)), with both ends inside the CDS.

At least 150 nt of CDS must remain. Trials 1-3 use seeds 1-3 for both the assignment and the cuts. The inputs are stranded, the tools were run as for fragments (CodAn partial models, RNAsamba partial weights) and the scoring is the same. For an internal fragment, a stop-level match means the prediction runs to the fragment end; an exact match means it also starts at the fragment start. Values are the median over organisms (seven for the tools without the ciliate code) in each trial, shown as the mean over the three trials (min-max over trials). The longest-ORF baseline is the longest ORF of the pytd_v7 LongOrfs run.

MX_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0", longest_orf = "longest ORF",
              prodigal = "Prodigal", gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
              cpc2 = "CPC2", borf = "Borf")
trial_of <- function(v) sub("fragments_mixed_", "", v)
MX_RAW <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "mixed_scores.tsv") %>% mutate(trial = trial_of(variant))
MX <- MX_RAW %>% filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE))
mr <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f (%.3f-%.3f)", mean(x), min(x), max(x))
mx_metrics <- c("sensitivity_stop", "precision_stop", "f1_stop", "sensitivity_exact", "precision_exact", "f1_exact")
mx_trial <- MX %>% filter(tool %in% names(MX_TOOLS)) %>% group_by(tool, trial) %>%
  summarise(n_org = n(), across(all_of(mx_metrics), median), .groups = "drop")
mx <- mx_trial %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(organisms = paste(unique(range(n_org)), collapse = "-"), trials = n(),
            across(all_of(mx_metrics), mr), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(method = factor(MX_TOOLS[tool], levels = MX_TOOLS)) %>% arrange(method) %>%
  select(method, organisms, trials, all_of(mx_metrics))
mx_mean <- mx_trial %>% group_by(tool) %>% summarise(across(all_of(mx_metrics), mean), .groups = "drop")
MXV <- function(tool, m) mx_mean[[m]][mx_mean$tool == tool]
mx_n <- MX %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% select(org, trial, n_truth) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = trial, values_from = n_truth)
mx_trial_spread <- mx_trial %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(mx_metrics), ~ max(.x) - min(.x)), .groups = "drop")
kable(mx, caption = "Balanced mixed inputs: all references, median over organisms, mean (range) over 3 trials")

Over the three trials the per-trial medians of every method and measure vary by at most 0.008 (largest range). TransDecoder: stop-level F1 0.970, exact F1 0.843; Prodigal 0.952 / 0.796; GeneMarkS-T 0.918 / 0.809; longest ORF 0.979 / 0.839.

By partial type (02_partial_types.py on the mixed inputs). Sensitivity is per type. Precision is over the predictions on sequences of that type, as in the previous section.

MPT <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "partial_types.tsv") %>%
  filter(grepl("^fragments_mixed_", variant), !(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE),
         tool %in% names(MX_TOOLS)) %>% mutate(trial = trial_of(variant))
TYPE_LABEL <- c(complete = "complete", `5prime_partial` = "5' partial", `3prime_partial` = "3' partial",
                internal = "internal")
mpt_trial <- MPT %>% group_by(tool, type, trial) %>%
  summarise(across(c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), median), .groups = "drop")
mpt_mean <- mpt_trial %>% group_by(tool, type) %>%
  summarise(across(c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), mean), .groups = "drop")
mpt_tab <- function(m) mpt_trial %>% group_by(tool, type) %>% summarise(v = mr(.data[[m]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(type = factor(TYPE_LABEL[type], levels = TYPE_LABEL), method = factor(MX_TOOLS[tool], levels = MX_TOOLS)) %>%
  arrange(type) %>% select(method, type, v) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = v) %>% arrange(method)
kable(mpt_tab("sensitivity_stop"), caption = "Stop-level sensitivity by type")

MPTV <- function(tool, type, m) mpt_mean[[m]][mpt_mean$tool == tool & mpt_mean$type == type]
f3p <- function(x) if (length(x) == 0) "(pending)" else f3(x)
codan_mx <- MX_RAW %>% filter(tool == "codan") %>% distinct(org, trial)

On internal fragments TransDecoder has stop-level sensitivity 0.940 and exact 0.783. Prodigal has 0.976 / 0.972, GeneMarkS-T 0.798 / 0.772 and CodAn (pending) / (pending) (CodAn: 0 of 21 runs scored so far; CodAn takes hours per input and its runs were still going when this was knitted; its rows appear in the tables once score_mixed.py and 02_partial_types.py are re-run). The ATG-requiring classifiers (CPAT, CPC2, RNAsamba, Borf) have stop-level sensitivity of at most 0.827 on internal fragments. The longest ORF of an internal fragment is almost always the reference frame, which has no stop codon, so the baseline is near 1 on this type by construction (1.000).

5’ partials by distance to the first in-frame ATG and by the share of the CDS removed (five_prime_by_distance.tsv, from score_mixed.py). On a 5’ partial an exact match means the prediction is left open at the fragment start. A stop-level match without an exact match usually means the prediction starts at a downstream ATG. “none”: no in-frame ATG in the remaining CDS.

FD <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "five_prime_by_distance.tsv") %>%
  filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE), tool %in% names(MX_TOOLS)) %>%
  mutate(trial = trial_of(variant))
fd_tab <- function(stratum_, m) {
  bins <- unique(FD$bin[FD$stratum == stratum_])
  FD %>% filter(stratum == stratum_) %>% group_by(tool, bin, trial) %>% summarise(v = median(.data[[m]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(tool, bin) %>% summarise(v = r3(mean(v)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(bin = factor(bin, levels = bins), method = factor(MX_TOOLS[tool], levels = MX_TOOLS)) %>% arrange(bin) %>%
    select(method, bin, v) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = bin, values_from = v) %>% arrange(method)
}
fd_n <- FD %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% group_by(stratum, bin, trial) %>% summarise(n = sum(n_truth), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(stratum, bin) %>% summarise(references = round(mean(n)), .groups = "drop")
kable(fd_tab("dist_first_inframe_atg", "sensitivity_exact"),
      caption = "5' partials: exact sensitivity (ORF left open) by nt from fragment start to first in-frame ATG")

FDV <- function(tool, b) {
  d <- FD %>% filter(stratum == "dist_first_inframe_atg", tool == !!tool, bin == b) %>% group_by(trial) %>%
    summarise(v = median(sensitivity_exact), .groups = "drop")
  mean(d$v)
}

TransDecoder leaves 0.668 of the 5’ partials open when an in-frame ATG lies within 30 nt of the fragment start, and 0.913 when the first in-frame ATG is 300 nt or more downstream. The corresponding values for Prodigal are 0.973 and 0.982.

Method rankings across inputs and measures

Each method is ranked in every combination of organism, stranded input (complete, complete with full UTRs, fragments, complete + random, fragments + random) and measure (stop-level and exact sensitivity, precision and F1): 7 organisms x 5 inputs x 6 measures = 210 categories. T. thermophila is left out, because five of the eight methods do not support its genetic code (above); it is compared separately under “Ciliate genetic code”. Only the methods run on all of these inputs are ranked: TransDecoder (release), Prodigal, GeneMarkS-T, CodAn, CPAT, CPC2, RNAsamba and Borf (RNAsamba was not run on unstranded inputs; v6.0.0 and the longest-ORF baseline are not ranked). Ties share the best rank. Because ranks ignore margins, the gap to the best method in each category (best value minus the method’s value) is reported too.

RANK_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", prodigal = "Prodigal", gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn",
                cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba", borf = "Borf")
RANK_INPUTS <- c(complete = "complete", complete_fullutr = "complete, full UTR", fragments = "fragments",
                 complete.wRand = "complete + random", fragments.wRand = "fragments + random")
RANK_MEASURES <- c(sensitivity_stop = "stop sensitivity", precision_stop = "stop precision",
                   f1_stop = "stop F1", sensitivity_exact = "exact sensitivity",
                   precision_exact = "exact precision", f1_exact = "exact F1")
rk <- S %>% filter(tool %in% names(RANK_TOOLS), variant %in% names(RANK_INPUTS)) %>%
  select(org, variant, tool, all_of(names(RANK_MEASURES))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(RANK_MEASURES)), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(org, variant, measure) %>% filter(n_distinct(tool) == length(RANK_TOOLS), !any(is.na(value))) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-value, ties.method = "min"), gap = max(value) - value) %>% ungroup()
n_cat <- n_distinct(rk %>% select(org, variant, measure))
rank_summary <- function(d) d %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(categories = n(), first = sum(rank == 1), top3 = sum(rank <= 3), median_rank = median(rank),
            within_0.01 = mean(gap <= 0.01), within_0.03 = mean(gap <= 0.03), median_gap = median(gap),
            max_gap = max(gap)) %>%
  mutate(method = RANK_TOOLS[tool]) %>% arrange(desc(first + top3 / 100))
rs_all <- rank_summary(rk)
rs_measure <- rk %>% group_by(measure, tool) %>%
  summarise(first = sum(rank == 1), top3 = sum(rank <= 3), median_rank = median(rank), .groups = "drop")
td_rs <- rs_all %>% filter(tool == TD)
td_gap <- rk %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% group_by(measure) %>%
  summarise(median_gap = median(gap), max_gap = max(gap), first = sum(rank == 1), top3 = sum(rank <= 3))
td_worst <- rk %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% slice_max(gap, n = 1)

Categories ranked: 210. TransDecoder ranks first in 50 (24%) and in the top three in 134 (64%), more than any other method; its median rank is 3. It is within 0.01 of the best method in 46% of categories and within 0.03 in 65%; its median gap to the best is 0.015 (next smallest: CPAT, 0.041). Its largest gap is 0.145 (A. thaliana, fragments + random, stop sensitivity). By measure, TransDecoder is never first in stop sensitivity (Prodigal is first in 22 of 35) and is first or tied first most often in stop F1 (16 of 35, median gap 0.004).

fmt_rs <- function(d) d %>% transmute(method, categories, first, `top 3` = top3, `median rank` = median_rank,
                                      `within 0.01` = pct(within_0.01, 0), `within 0.03` = pct(within_0.03, 0),
                                      `median gap` = f3(median_gap), `max gap` = f3(max_gap))

  count(method, bin)
pa <- ggplot(rank_bins, aes(n, method, fill = forcats::fct_rev(bin))) + geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`1` = "#08519c", `2` = "#4292c6", `3` = "#9ecae1", `4-8` = "#e5e5e5"),
                    breaks = c("1", "2", "3", "4-8"), name = "rank") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 70, 140, 210)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("categories (of %d)", n_cat), y = NULL, title = "rank in each category")
heat_r <- rs_measure %>% mutate(method = factor(RANK_TOOLS[tool], levels = rev(tool_order)),
                                measure = factor(RANK_MEASURES[measure], levels = RANK_MEASURES))
pb <- ggplot(heat_r, aes(measure, method, fill = median_rank)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d/%d", first, top3)), size = 1.55,
            colour = ifelse(heat_r$median_rank <= 3, "white", "#222222")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#08519c", high = "#f0f0f0", limits = c(1, 8), name = "median rank") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "first / top 3 (of 35), by measure") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
pc <- ggplot(rk %>% mutate(method = factor(RANK_TOOLS[tool], levels = rev(tool_order))),
             aes(pmax(gap, 1e-4), method)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, linewidth = 0.25, fill = "#deebf7") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1e-4, 1e-2, 1), labels = c("0", "0.01", "1")) +
  labs(x = "gap to best (log)", y = NULL, title = "gap to best")
figS4 <- (pa + pb + pc) + plot_layout(widths = c(0.9, 1.5, 0.8)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title.position = "top", legend.key.width = unit(4, "mm"))

Simulated GM12878 Trinity assembly

A benchmark on assembled transcripts whose true coding regions are known (E30; scripts pipeline/simtrinity/, tables data/simtrinity/). Reads were simulated from annotated transcripts only, at GM12878 expression levels, and assembled with the pipeline used for the real GM12878 Trinity assembly (E11). So the input has the fragment, isoform and chimera structure of a real genome-guided Trinity assembly, while every contig can be traced to its source transcript.

  • Transcripts simulated: GENCODE v50 protein_coding transcripts with a complete CDS (no *_NF tags; ATG to stop, a whole number of codons, no internal stop) and all lncRNA transcripts. Nothing else: no pre-mRNA, retained-intron, NMD or pseudogene transcripts.
  • Expression: salmon 1.10.3 counts (ISR, --seqBias --gcBias, full GENCODE v50 index) from the real reads (ENCSR000AED rep 1); the rounded counts of the kept transcripts are simulated.
  • Reads: Polyester 1.38.0, paired 101 nt, illumina5 errors, fragment length from salmon, stranded with read 1 antisense (dUTP/RF, as the real library).
  • Assembly: STAR 2-pass (same index and parameters as the real run; run on methods02 for memory), Trinity 2.15.2 genome-guided (--SS_lib_type RF --min_kmer_cov 2), minimap2 splice:hq to GRCh38.
  • Labels (label_assembly.py): a contig is compatible with a simulated transcript when their exons agree over the overlap (same introns; up to 10 nt of terminal overhang tolerated). The source CDS is projected onto compatible contigs, which are labelled complete, 5’ partial, 3’ partial or internal from the CDS ends they contain; contigs compatible only with lncRNAs and overlapping no GENCODE CDS are negatives. Contigs with conflicting projections (ambiguous), fewer than 50 codons (short) or no resolvable structure (unresolved) stay in the input, but predictions on them are not scored.
  • Scoring: as for the other inputs (score_predictions.py): stop within 2 nt, exact when the start is also within 2 nt, one credit per truth CDS; every prediction on a negative is a false positive. The input is named fragments_simtrinity.fa, so run_tool.sh treats it as stranded and as fragments (RNAsamba partial-length weights); CPAT uses the human model. CodAn was not run (too slow) and perl_td_v7 was not run (identical to pytd_v7 on all other inputs; E08, E25).
ST <- function(f) read_tab("simtrinity", f)
sim_par <- ST("sim_params.tsv") %>% { setNames(.[[2]], .[[1]]) }
sim_sel <- read_tsv(data_path("simtrinity", "selection_counts.tsv"), col_names = c("step", "n"), show_col_types = FALSE)
SEL <- setNames(sim_sel$n, sim_sel$step)
asm <- ST("assembly_stats.tsv")
ASM <- function(m, w = "simulated") asm[[w]][asm$metric == m]
LC <- ST("label_counts.tsv")
lc_n <- function(a, l) sum(LC$n[LC$assembly == a & LC$label %in% l])
SCORED_TYPES <- c("complete", "5prime_partial", "3prime_partial", "internal")
lab_tab <- LC %>% mutate(group = case_when(label %in% SCORED_TYPES ~ "coding (truth)", label == "noncoding" ~ "negative",
                                           TRUE ~ "not scored")) %>%
  group_by(assembly, group, label) %>% summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(assembly) %>% mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()

Labels. The real GM12878 Trinity assembly was labelled with the same script against the same transcript set, for comparison (its contigs come from all transcripts, pre-mRNA and unannotated isoforms, so most are unresolved there).

Of 84,972 simulated contigs, 33,939 carry a scored CDS, 20,815 are negatives and 27,666 (32.6%) are unresolved. The two largest unresolved groups are contigs compatible with coding transcripts but holding only UTR sequence (13,447) and contigs whose intron chain matches no single simulated transcript (12,137; half of them annotated introns joined in new combinations by the assembler). Among the scored contigs, 83.1% are complete in the simulated assembly against 67.9% in the real one. The E29 statistic (contigs carrying a MANE Select stop with the reference structure to their 5’ end that begin inside the CDS) is 7.0% simulated vs 13.6% real: the simulated assembly is more complete than the real one (uniform coverage, no pre-mRNA, no degradation).

TransDecoder: stop-level F1 0.916, exact F1 0.844, with a prediction on 8.1% of the lncRNA-derived negatives. Prodigal finds more stops (sensitivity 0.978) but predicts on 51.8% of the negatives (exact F1 0.453); the longest-ORF baseline predicts on 70.6% of them. CPAT and RNAsamba reach stop F1 0.901 and 0.900 but cannot leave a 5’ end open (exact sensitivity on 5’ partials and internal fragments below 0.02).

SIM_TYPE_LAB <- c(complete = "complete", `5prime_partial` = "5' partial", `3prime_partial` = "3' partial",
                  internal = "internal")
TYPE_COL <- c(complete = COMPLETE_C, `5' partial` = "#fd8d3c", `3' partial` = "#fdd0a2", internal = FRAG_C)
pa <- LC %>% filter(label %in% SCORED_TYPES) %>% group_by(assembly) %>% mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(type = factor(SIM_TYPE_LAB[label], levels = rev(SIM_TYPE_LAB)),
         assembly = factor(assembly, c("simulated", "real"), c("sim.", "real"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(assembly, frac, fill = type)) + geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TYPE_COL, breaks = unname(SIM_TYPE_LAB), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = percent) + labs(x = NULL, y = "scored contigs", title = "CDS type") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
pb <- so %>% left_join(neg, by = "tool") %>% select(method, f1_stop, f1_exact, frac_negatives_with_pred) %>%
  pivot_longer(-method) %>%
  mutate(name = factor(name, c("f1_stop", "f1_exact", "frac_negatives_with_pred"),
                       c("stop F1", "exact F1", "negatives\npredicted on")), method = factor(method, rev(SIM_TOOLS))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, method, fill = method == "TransDecoder")) + geom_col(width = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~name, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = TD_C, `FALSE` = GREY), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1"), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "all scored contigs")
pc <- sbe %>% filter(tool %in% c(TD, "prodigal", "gmst", "cpat", "longest_orf")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(tpm_bin, sensitivity_exact, colour = method, group = method)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(TransDecoder = TD_C, Prodigal = "#d95f02", `GeneMarkS-T` = "#7570b3", CPAT = "#1b9e77",
                                 `longest ORF` = GREY), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "source TPM", y = "exact sensitivity", title = "by expression") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1)) + guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
figS_sim <- (pa + pb + pc) + plot_layout(widths = c(0.6, 2, 1.5)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(figS_sim, "figS_simtrinity", FULL_W, 85 * MM)
figS_sim

Checks against the manuscript

Each row compares a value computed here with the value in the text now. Labels give the tex file and line (mb = methods_benchmark.tex, rb = results_benchmark.tex, fm = figures_main.tex). TransDecoder values are from the release runs, so TransDecoder mismatches are expected until the text is updated (see the previous section for the earlier values).
